title: Iran War Exposes Shortcomings in U.S. Military Industrial Base
partialText: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is taking on a problem that the Pentagon and Congress have tried, and mostly failed, to address for years.

title: Trump Says He Postponed a ‘Very Major Attack’ on Iran, Leaving Mideast on Edge
partialText: President Trump threatened “another big hit” on Iran, saying the country had days to return to the negotiating table, as Pakistan continued its mediation efforts to end the war.

title: Inflation Fears Cloud G7 Economic Agenda as Iran War Persists
partialText: The United States and Europe were at odds over the Trump administration’s decision to ease oil sanctions on Russia.

title: The IRS Thought it Could Fight Trump’s Lawsuit, but it Reached a Deal Anyway
partialText: Officials wrote a memo outlining ways to challenge President Trump’s suit against the Internal Revenue Service. The administration is instead creating an “anti-weaponization” fund.

title: Before the San Diego Mosque Shooting, a Fearful Mother’s Phone Call Set Off a Frantic Search
partialText: San Diego police arrived to find three people dead. Nearby, they found two teenagers, the attackers, dead in a car. The violence shattered an idyllic Southern California city.

title: San Diego Mosque Shooting: What to Know About the Suspects and What Happened
partialText: Three men were killed in the attack at the Islamic Center of San Diego. Two teenage suspects were found dead in a car nearby, police said.

title: A Generational Fracture Emerges for Republicans Over Foreign Policy
partialText: Younger Republicans are less likely to support overseas interventions and aid, a Times/Siena poll shows.

title: G.O.P. Supporters Back Trump, but a Third Seek a New Direction for the Party
partialText: While President Trump remains overwhelmingly popular within the Republican coalition, a New York Times/Siena poll found, a sizable share wants the party’s next nominee to take a different approach.

title: What to Watch in Tuesday’s Primary Elections in Kentucky, Georgia and Beyond
partialText: A prominent Republican critic of President Trump is trying to hang on in Kentucky, and other states are also holding primaries that will test Mr. Trump’s power over his party.

title: Justices Hint at Strains as Supreme Court Comes Under Scrutiny
partialText: Traveling across the country, justices defend the role of the court even as strained relations among its members emerge in writing and remarks.

title: How Trump Entrusted His World Cup to Another Giuliani
partialText: Andrew Giuliani, the son of Rudy and a longtime Trump loyalist, is overseeing American hosting duties for the World Cup next month. It’s a big promotion.

title: ‘The Future of Truth’ Contains Quotes Made Up by A.I.
partialText: Steven Rosenbaum, author of “The Future of Truth,” said he had started his own investigation after The New York Times asked about the fake quotes.

title: China Wants A.I. to Flourish, but Not at the Expense of Jobs
partialText: A series of precedent-setting rulings signals that Chinese courts are being enlisted to shield workers from displacement by artificial intelligence.

title: On Blind, Anxious Tech Workers Get the Lowdown on Layoffs
partialText: On the website Blind, professionals share advice — and gallows humor — anonymously. It is chronicling the curdling of tech optimism.

title: As a Weakened Putin Follows Trump to Beijing, Iran War Offers an Opening
partialText: With the upheaval in the Persian Gulf disrupting oil and gas supplies, Russia is looking to deepen its energy ties to China.

title: As Ukraine Strikes Russian Oil Sites, an Environmental Disaster Unfolds
partialText: After invading more than four years ago, Moscow has usually been the one causing ecological disaster. But Kyiv’s strikes, intended to cut into the Kremlin’s oil revenue, have flipped the script.

title: Ebola Outbreak in Central Africa Could Last Months, W.H.O. Says
partialText: Health officials reported more than 130 suspected deaths and 513 cases, a sharp rise since the outbreak was identified on May 15 in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda.

title: What to Know About the Ebola Outbreak as Cases and Deaths Rise
partialText: More than 130 deaths and over 500 cases are suspected. The United States restricted entry for people who have been to three African countries after a global health emergency was declared.

title: Tesla’s Semi Truck could Jolt the Trucking Industry
partialText: California truckers have expressed strong interest in the Tesla Semi because it costs much less and can travel further on a charge than electric trucks sold by established manufacturers.

title: Amazon E-Bikes Take Root in Manhattan and Brooklyn
partialText: Small companies that handle the final delivery are relying on them to skirt New York City traffic. Amazon plans to try the bikes elsewhere, too.

title: Bipartisan Bill Would Impose New Annual Fee on Electric Vehicles
partialText: A House transportation bill introduced this week would require owners of electric cars to pay $130 to cover the cost of road repairs.

title: Woman Dies After Falling Into Open Manhole in Manhattan
partialText: The woman had parked her S.U.V., then got out and plunged 10 feet into the uncovered hole managed by Con Edison, prompting an investigation.

title: The Best of ‘S.N.L.’ Season 51: Sensitive Strippers and Regretful Moms
partialText: This season “Saturday Night Live” found new ways to satirize the Trump administration and said goodbye to one of its most valuable cast members.

title: How to End the Gerrymandering Doom Loop Forever
partialText: The political scientist Lee Drutman argues that we should switch to a system of proportional representation and put an end to our “trench warfare politics.”

title: The Race to Control Congress
partialText: We look at where the parties stand leading up to the midterms.

title: How Has Your Shopping Changed in the Era of Weight-Loss Drugs?
partialText: In the last few years, weight-loss drugs like Ozempic have altered how many Americans think about clothes and getting dressed.

title: Israeli Minister Threatens to Evict Palestinians From West Bank Hamlet
partialText: Bezalel Smotrich, the hard-line minister, said he was retaliating for the International Criminal Court seeking his arrest, something the court did not confirm nor deny.

title: Twist in FIFA Corruption Case: 2 Fugitives Emerge, Seeking a Plea Deal
partialText: Federal prosecutors are negotiating with Hugo and Mariano Jinkis, a father and son from Argentina, who after more than a decade suddenly agreed to meet in Brooklyn.
